items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: I says, 'Who's Picasso?', the painter... I made a mistake there, I was thinkin' about Pablo Casals, not Pablo Picasso

ctx.x: Jimmy Rochelle. So we come to Chicago, on a holiday, and I caught Coleman in person for the first time at Dave's Cafe which was at 55th and Garfield. And I heard that sound. Now, what actually I heard was that every note that he played...they were all the same bigness, all the notes. I says, "Ohhhh, ohhhhh," because the other tenor players, they had certain notes that they petted and they became bigger, but all of his notes were big. And it was really somethin'. When they do the show he came out from the kitchen…

what I mean, 'cause this is the way he lives, you see. So that was another lesson. So, after I heard him, I says, "Well, look, I'm gonna...", then I started listening to Lester for his rhythm and whatnot. But then I became more aware that Coleman was...and the way people loved him and the way they loved Ben Webster and I could see that this is the type of thing I wanted to do. Then I found out, even when I was at home, Coleman Hawkins had an article in some magazine, I don't know where my father found it, but the…

on sound, ya dig what I mean? So when I learned how to...I went into opera singers and I found out how they would breath so I became curious about...how Coleman... he also...oh, oh...I made a mistake there, I was thinkin' about Pablo Casals, not Pablo Picasso, he wanted to do some unaccompanied things like Pablo Casals...but...
